original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
— Pick, price approval outstanding

Main case: **Martator**, ranked first, finished two lengths behind Vanderpoel over this C&D on 31 October. He then carried 168 lb against 165; now 167 against 168, so he is **4 lb better off**. His Grand Annual win is additional demonstrated chase class. Second-ranked **Calico** won this race last year; 168 minus his verified 10 lb claim = **158 lb**, versus Vanderpoel’s 168. The claim matters, but a claim is not a guaranteed improvement in performance and recent form has been less convincing. Third-ranked **Ryan’s Rocket**, 159 lb, won the Red Rum; his 9 lb receipt offsets a 9 lb rating gap and he also returns from a break. **Shakeyatailfeather**, 143 minus 5 = 138 lb, has a route after being left too much to do in the same C&D race and an early unseat subsequently. **Sans Bruit**, 153 minus 5 = 148 lb, is a credible pace participant but has been less effective in this race; **Gabriel’s Getaway**, 142 lb, is 4 lb out of the handicap.

Strongest winning case: Vanderpoel won decisively here after wind surgery, is still improving in his second chase season and may overcome a 7 lb rise. This is not a lay because he is progressive. The verdict survives because Martator’s exact direct comparison and Calico’s meaningful claim provide independent concrete opposition. This makes it a Pick on its own race evidence, not a promotion of an unvalidated Watchlist theory. Bet365 screening 2.75; later Sporting Life showed 6/4. Value remains unproven.

The proposed 4 lb swing did not reverse their previous order. Calico fell and Ryan’s Rocket was explicitly BroughtDown on Sporting Life; Racing API uses F for Ryan’s Rocket. Retain that provider distinction and prefer the explicit Sporting Life casualty evidence. These casualties limit evaluation of the full three-rival case, not settlement of Vanderpoel’s win. Sans Bruit, outside the principal three, came closest. Running comments were blank, so do not invent how Vanderpoel won or the timing/cause of the casualties. Recognised post-wind-operation progress remained consequential; neither a 7 lb rise nor a claim guaranteed vulnerability.
